stem_en: Given below are two statements: Statement I: The boiling point of hydrides of Group 16 elements follow the order $\mathrm{H2O}$ > $\mathrm{H2Te}$ > $\mathrm{H2Se}$ > $\mathrm{H2S}$. Statement II: On the basis of molecular mass, $\mathrm{H\ 2O}$ is expected to have lower boiling point than the other members of the group but due to the presence of extensive H-bonding in $\mathrm{H2O}$, it has higher boiling point. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

statements.label: Statement I
statements.text: The boiling point of hydrides of Group 16 elements follow the order $\mathrm{H2O}$ > $\mathrm{H2Te}$ > $\mathrm{H2Se}$ > $\mathrm{H2S}$.

statements.label: Statement II
statements.text: On the basis of molecular mass, $\mathrm{H\ 2O}$ is expected to have lower boiling point than the other members of the group but due to the presence of extensive H-bonding in $\mathrm{H2O}$, it has higher boiling point.

options_en.1: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
options_en.2: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
options_en.3: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
options_en.4: Statement I is false but Statement II is true

b6_reason: The order H2O > H2Te > H2Se > H2S is the correct observed one, and extensive H-bonding in water is the correct reason for its anomalously high value.
b6_working: bp: H2O 373 K, H2Te 271 K, H2Se 232 K, H2S 213 K. After H2S the bp rises with molecular mass (van der Waals forces); H2O breaks the trend because of H-bonding.
